page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.n1.7xlarge is an x86_64 server instance powered by an Intel Xeon 8163 processor clocked at 2.5 GHz. The configuration allocates 32 vCPUs across 16 physical cores via simultaneous multithreading (2 threads per core) with dedicated CPU scheduling on the KVM hypervisor. System memory totals 64.0 GB, yielding a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. The instance does not include GPU hardware accelerators or local ephemeral storage, requiring workloads to depend on attached network volumes for persistent storage.

Benchmark results demonstrate a clear difference between single-threaded efficiency and parallel compute capabilities. Single-core throughput is constrained, registering a Geekbench single-core score of 910.0, a stress-ng single-core rating of 1099.89, and gzip single-threaded compression at 19.09 GB/sec. Conversely, multi-threaded results align with median tier expectations, achieving 29309.22 in stress-ng multi-core, 8155.0 in Geekbench multi-core, and a PassMark CPU score of 27781.64. The instance also achieved 31.14 million Redis SET operations per second and 15.19 GB/sec in static web serving throughput.

Uncached memory bandwidth measures 88.67 GB/sec for reads and 47.18 GB/sec for writes across 256 MB blocks, accompanied by a PassMark memory score of 1831.83. The hardware profile exhibits a resource-dense CPU layout relative to memory capacity, making it cost-efficient for parallel tasks that do not require high per-core burst capacity or local NVMe speeds. Workloads best aligned with this configuration include parallel code compilation, containerized web frontends, multi-threaded batch processors, and distributed caching services.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.n1.7xlarge is a compute-oriented x86_64 virtual instance powered by a 2.5 GHz Intel Xeon 8163 processor. It provides 32 dedicated vCPUs across 16 physical cores paired with 64.0 GB of memory, delivering a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. The instance does not bundle GPU acceleration or local ephemeral storage. Synthetic benchmarks indicate lower-tier single-threaded output, including a Geekbench single-core score of 910.0 and stress-ng single-core score of 1099.89. In contrast, parallel benchmarks meet mid-tier standards, highlighted by 29309.22 in stress-ng multi-core, 27781.64 in PassMark CPU, and 15.19 GB/sec static web serving throughput. Lacking local disks but maintaining strong multi-threaded execution, the instance is suitable for parallel software builds, distributed batch compute, web serving pools, and horizontally scaled microservices.
